restatement: Make one mutable registry of filter definitions the single source for render, spec() and analyze/validate. Filters take and return values, and the six existing filters coerce to text first, so no existing template output changes. Filter calls are parsed once at parse time with quotes respected, so fence="a=b" keeps its whole language. A named parameter a filter does not declare is a located type-error. An unterminated quote in a ?? default no longer swallows the later filters. Two empty group files feed the registry for later cards. No existing test expectation changes beyond the spec test, no runtime dependency is added, and no template text is evaluated as code.
verification_plan: c1: confirm render, spec() and analyze/validate all read FILTER_REGISTRY at call time, with no load-time copy and no second name list, and that spec() maps to name, params and description only.
c1: check that a definition pushed into the registry and later removed is seen, then unseen, by all three consumers.

c2: check that each of the six filters coerces input exactly as the output step does. Check that non-string values reach a custom filter unchanged and that its return value is printed like an unfiltered value.
c3: check that parse-time filter parsing splits on | and on = or : only outside quotes, and that parseFilter keeps its old results for old strings.
c3: check that an undeclared named parameter gives a type-error at the variable's line and column in strict and lenient mode, and that validate and analyze agree with render.
c4: check that an unterminated quote in a ?? default no longer swallows later filters, and that a closed quoted default still hides its pipe.
c5: check that filters-text.ts and filters-collection.ts export empty arrays that the registry spreads in.
c6/m1: check that only tests/headless/spec.test.ts changed among existing tests.
m2: look for any path where existing filter output or default-value handling changes.
m3/m4: look for new imports or dependencies and for any eval or Function use.
